chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man from my uncle's sons, who is among the virtuous of your mawali, ordered me to ask you about al-nabidh and describe it to you.' He said: 'I will describe it to you. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Every intoxicant is forbidden, and that which makes much of it intoxicates, little of it is also forbidden.
He said. I said: 'Then does a large amount of water make the small amount of the forbidden thing permissible?' He replied to me with his two hands twice, saying: 'No, no.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on small amounts of intoxicants if the large amount is forbidden?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Muawiya ibn Wahb seeks clarification on *nabidh* (fermented drink) from Imam al-Sadiq, who cites the Prophet’s foundational principle: 'Every intoxicant is forbidden.' The Imam’s emphatic double gesture ('an la, la') when asked if dilution renders the small amount permissible underscores the Shia scholarly consensus that the essence of the substance remains impure regardless of quantity or concentration, rejecting the notion that mere dilution purifies the intoxicant.
